Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 2. Big happy family
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: My little friend
- Materials: Photos, object cards, lost-property box, COSYmanuals 'possessive adjectives' and 'possessive 's' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• use possessive adjectives my, your, his, her, our, their
• express possession using 's

Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

my — belonging to me. Example: This is my bag.
your — belonging to you. Example: Is this your phone?
his — belonging to a man or boy. Example: His name is Omar.
her — belonging to a woman or girl. Example: Her bag is red.
our — belonging to us. Example: Our house is small.
their — belonging to them. Example: Their children are at school.
cousin — a child of your aunt or uncle. Example: My cousin lives in London.
uncle — the brother of your mother or father. Example: My uncle is very funny.
aunt — the sister of your mother or father. Example: My aunt lives near us.
relative — a person in your family. Example: We visit our relatives at Eid.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• This is my cousin. (introducing a family member)
• Her name is Sarah. (giving a name)
• His uncle is nice. (describing a relative)
• Our aunt lives in a small house. (talking about a relative's home)
• Their children are at school. (talking about another family)
• Whose bag is this? (asking about possession)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'belonging to me'?
Which word means 'belonging to you'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Possessive adjective vowels and the /ð/ sound in 'their'

my /maɪ/ — long /aɪ/
her /hɜː/ — long /ɜː/
our /aʊə/ — two vowel sounds
their /ðeə/ — voiced th
Listen and repeat:
This is my cousin. Her name is Sarah. Their children are at school.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use possessive adjectives to say who something belongs to.

Form:
Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their + noun. They do not change with the noun: 'my books', 'her book'.

Examples:
• This is my bag.
• Her name is Sara.
• Our house is small.
• Their children are at school.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
This is ___ bag. (I)
___ name is Omar. (he)
___ house is big. (we)
The children love ___ school. (they)
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• This is ... (my / your / his) phone.
• ... (Her / His / Their) name is Maria.
• We love ... (our / their / her) city.
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• Whose bag is this?
• What is your favourite place in your city?
• Who is your best friend?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your family with possessive adjectives.
• Write three sentences about your things with possessive adjectives.
Reading: My little friend

This is my little friend. Her name is Sarah. She is my cousin. Her mother is my aunt, and her father is my uncle. They live in a small house near our home. Sarah's brother is at school. His name is Adam. Their dog is very friendly. We play together every weekend.
Who is Sarah?
Whose dog is friendly?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Is this your bag?
B: No, it isn't. It's my cousin's bag.
A: What is her name?
B: Her name is Sarah. That is her brother, Adam.
A: And is this their dog?
B: Yes, it is. Their dog is very friendly.
Whose bag is it?
What is the cousin's name?
Speaking task: Show your partner three photos or drawings of family/friends. Say who they are and whose things are in the picture.

• Who is your favourite relative?
• Whose house do you visit most often?
• What is your cousin's name?
• Do you share things with your family?
• Whose phone is on the table?
Role-play: You are at a family gathering. Introduce your cousin and uncle to a friend, and answer questions about whose bag and phone are on the table.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about a friend or relative using possessive adjectives and 's.
Model: This is my ... His/Her name is ... His/Her ... is ... Our ... Their ...
